en: It is the Peace of Westphalia that has fixed this relation of the independence of the parts.

For themselves they would not have been capable of it; rather their league was scattered to dust, and they themselves and their lands, without the possibility of a resistance of their own, were in the political and religious despot's hand of Ferdinand.
zh: 正是《威斯特伐利亚和约》把各部分这种独立的关系固定了下来。
单靠他们自己本来做不到这一点；他们的联盟早已散成粉末，他们自己和他们的土地，连自己抵抗一下的可能都没有，全落在斐迪南那只政治和宗教上的专制者手里。

en: Gustav Adolf's own expedition would, not in regard to his person - for he died at the height of good fortune -, but in regard to his nation, have been placed in a completely same class with his descendant Charles XII.
expeditions.
Swedish power likewise succumbed in Germany, if Richelieu's policy, which Mazarin carried out in the same sense, had not taken up and sustained its cause.
zh: 古斯塔夫·阿道夫本人的远征，就他这个人来说——因为他死在了幸运的顶点——本来不会，但就他的民族来说，本来会与他的后人卡尔十二世的远征完全同列。
……的远征。
瑞典的势力在德意志同样也垮掉了，若不是黎塞留的政策——马扎林以同样的用意把它实行下去——接过了它的事业并把它维持下来的话。

en: Richelieu was granted the rare good fortune of having been held to be their greatest benefactor both by that state to whose greatness he laid the true ground and by that one at whose expense it happened.
zh: 黎塞留得到了那种罕见的幸运：无论是他为其强大奠定了真正基础的那个国家，还是为此付出代价的那个国家，都把他看作自己最大的恩人。

en: France as state and Germany as state both had in themselves the same two principles of dissolution; in the one he destroyed them completely and thereby raised it to one of the most powerful states, in the other he gave them all power and thereby abolished its existence as a state.

In both countries he brought the principle on which they were inwardly founded fully to ripeness: the principle of France, monarchy; the principle of Germany, the formation of a multitude of separate states.
Both still had to struggle with their opposite [principle]; Richelieu succeeded in bringing both countries to their firm, mutually opposed system.
zh: 法国作为国家、德意志作为国家，自身都含有同样两条解体的原则；在其中一个里，他把这两条原则彻底毁掉，从而把它抬成了最强大的国家之一；在另一个里，他却把全部权力交给了它们，从而取消了它作为国家的存在。
在两个国家里，他都把它们内在地奠基于其上的那条原则彻底带向了成熟：法国的原则是君主制，德意志的原则是形成众多自己的国家。
两者都还得同自己那条相反的原则搏斗；黎塞留做到了把两个国家带到它们各自稳固的、彼此相反的制度上去。

en: The two principles that hindered France from becoming a state in the form of a monarchy were the great nobles and the Huguenots; both waged wars with the kings.
zh: 阻碍法国成为一个君主制形式的国家的两条原则，是大贵族和胡格诺派；两者都同国王们打仗。

en: The great nobles, to whom the members of the royal family also [belonged], intrigued with armies against the minister.

True, sovereignty had long been sacred to the monarch and exalted above all claims, and the great nobles did not lead armies into the field in order to assert a sovereignty for themselves, but in order to be, as ministers, governors of provinces, etc., the first subjects of the monarchs.
Richelieu's merit of having subjected the great nobles to the state power in its first emanations, the ministry, has, considered superficially, the appearance of ambition.

Those who were his enemies seem to have fallen as victims of his ambition; in their revolts and conspiracies they protested, and probably with the greatest truth, their innocence and their devotion to duty toward their sovereign, and regarded resistance by arms against the person of the minister as neither a civil nor a state crime.
But they succumbed not to the person of Richelieu but to his genius, which bound his person to the necessary principle of the unity of the state and made state offices dependent on the state.
And political genius consists in this, that the individual identifies himself with a principle; in this union he must necessarily carry off the victory.

As the merit of a minister, what Richelieu has done, namely to have given unity to the executive state power, is infinitely more exalted than the merit of having enlarged a country by one province or otherwise rescued it from distress.
zh: 大贵族——王室的成员也算在其内——带着军队搞阴谋，反对这位宰相。
的确，主权早已被奉为君主所有、高居于一切要求之上；大贵族带兵上阵，并不是要为自己争得一份主权，而是要作为宰相、各省总督等等，做君主的第一批臣民。
黎塞留的功劳在于使大贵族服从国家权力最初的表现形态即宰相府；乍看上去，这功劳带着野心的假象。
那些与他为敌的人，看来是作为他野心的牺牲品倒下的；他们在自己的暴动和阴谋中一再申明自己对君主的无辜和忠于职守——这大概也最合乎真理——并且认为用武器对抗宰相本人，既不算市民的罪，也不算国家的罪。
但他们败给的并不是黎塞留这个人，而是他的天才；这种天才把他个人同国家统一这一必然原则绑在一起，使国家官职依附于国家。
政治天才就在这里：个人把自己同一条原则等同起来；在这种结合中，他必然要取得胜利。
作为一位宰相的功劳，黎塞留所做的，也就是使执行的国家权力获得统一，这远远高出于把一国扩大一个省、或者把它从别的困境中解救出来的功劳。

en: The other principle threatening a dissolution of the state was the Huguenots, whom Richelieu suppressed as a political party; his procedure against them does not fall at all under the point of view of a suppression of freedom of conscience.

They had their own armies, fortified cities, alliances with foreign powers, etc., and accordingly formed a kind of sovereign state; in opposition to them the great nobles had formed the League, which had brought the French state to the edge of the abyss.
Both opposing parties were an armed fanaticism and exalted above the state power.

In destroying the state of the Huguenots, Richelieu at the same time destroyed the right of a League, and he finished off the remaining fragment of it, devoid of right and principle, the insubordination of the great nobles.
In exterminating the state of the Huguenots he left them freedom of conscience, churches, divine service, civil and political rights, equal with the Catholics.

Through his consistency as a statesman he found and practised tolerance, which more than centuries later was put forward as the product of a more educated humanity and as the most brilliant merit of philosophy and of the softening of manners; and it was not ignorance and fanaticism of the French if in the war and in the Peace of Westphalia they did not think of the separation of the state and the church in Germany and made religion the ground of a distinction of political and civil rights and asserted in Germany a principle that they abolished in their own country.
zh: 另一条威胁国家解体的原则是胡格诺派，黎塞留把他们当作一个政治党派加以压制；他对付他们的做法，根本不属于压制良心的自由这个角度。
他们有自己军队、设防城市、同外国势力的结盟等等，因此构成了一种主权的国家；大贵族则与他们相对立，组成了联盟，这联盟曾把法国带到深渊的边缘。
两个对立的派别都是武装起来的狂热，都高踞于国家权力之上。
黎塞留在摧毁胡格诺派的国家时，也就同时摧毁了一个联盟的权利；而它剩下的那点既无权利又无原则的东西，即大贵族的不服从，他也收拾掉了。
在铲除胡格诺派的国家时，他留给他们良心的自由、教会、礼拜，以及同天主教徒平等的市民权利和政治权利。
凭着他作为政治家的彻底一贯，他发现并实行了宽容——这种做法在几百年以后才被说成是更有教养的人类的产物，是哲学和风俗软化最光彩的功劳；法国人在战争中和《威斯特伐利亚和约》里没有想到德意志的国家与教会的分离，反而把宗教当作区分政治权利和市民权利的根据，在德意志推行一种他们自己国内已经取消的原则，这并不是法国人的无知和狂热。

en: Thus France, also England, Spain and the other European countries, have succeeded in bringing to rest and to union the elements fermenting within them and threatening to shatter the state, and, through the freedom of the feudal constitution which Germania [showed] them, in attaining to a centre determined according to laws through freedom and gathering all forces - the properly monarchical or modern republican form, which however also falls under the principle of the limited, i.e. law-based monarchy, is here indifferent - and from this epoch of the formation of the countries into a state dates the period of the power, of the wealth of the state and of the free, lawful prosperity of individuals.
zh: 这样，法国、还有英国、西班牙和其他欧洲国家，都成功地把它们内部发酵、并威胁要砸碎国家的那些因素带向安宁和结合，并且凭借封建采邑制的那种自由——日耳曼尼亚[向他们展示了这种自由]——达到一个按法律、通过自由来规定的、汇集一切力量的中心——真正君主制的形式或现代共和制的形式，不过它们也属于有限君主制即建立在法律之上的君主制这条原则，在这里无关紧要——；而从各国形成为国家的这个时期起，就开始了一个国家权力、国家财富以及个人自由而合法的富裕的时期。

en: With Germany, by contrast, Italy has had the same course of fate in common, only that Italy, because a greater culture already lay in it beforehand, led its fate earlier to the development toward which Germany is wholly heading.
zh: 与德意志相反，意大利同它共有同一条命运的进程，只不过意大利因为它那里早先就有更高的教养，更早地把自己的命运引向了那种发展，而德意志正完全朝着那种发展走去。

en: Over Italy the Roman-German emperors long asserted a supremacy which, as in Germany, ordinarily had only as much force, and only then, as was asserted through the emperor's own power.
The emperors' craving to keep both countries under their rule has destroyed their power in both.
zh: 对意大利，罗马-德意志的皇帝们长期主张一种至上权，这种权力和在德意志一样，通常只有那么多力量，而且只有靠皇帝自己的力量去主张它时才有力量。
皇帝们贪求把这两个国家都留在自己的统治之下，这毁掉了他们在两个国家里的权力。

en: In Italy every point of it acquired sovereignty for itself; it ceased to be a state and became a throng of independent states, monarchies, aristocracies, democracies, as chance would have it; even the degeneration of these constitutions into tyranny, oligarchy and ochlocracy came to light for a short time.
The condition of Italy cannot be called anarchy, for the mass of the opposed parties were organized states.
Despite the lack of a proper state association, a large part always united for common resistance against the head of the empire, just as the other part did in order to make common cause with him.

The Ghibelline and Guelph party, which formerly embraced Germany as well as Italy, presented themselves in Germany in the 18th century - with modifications that arise from changed circumstances of the time - as the Austrian and Prussian party.
zh: 在意大利，它的每一点都为自己争得了主权；它不再是一个国家，而变成了一堆各自独立的国家——君主国、贵族制、民主制，全凭偶然；这些宪法蜕变成僭主制、寡头制和暴民统治，也曾在短时间内露过头。
意大利的状况不能叫做无政府状态，因为那些相互对立的大量派别都是些有组织的国家。
尽管缺少一个真正的国家联合体，总有一大部分联合起来，共同抵抗帝国的最高首脑，而另一部分也联合起来，要和他结成共同的事业。
从前既包括德意志也包括意大利的吉伯林党和归尔甫党，在18世纪的德意志——带着由时代境况改变而来的种种变化——是作为奥地利党和普鲁士党出现的。

en: The individual parts of Italy had not long dissolved the previous state and raised themselves up to independence when they provoked the conquering greed of greater powers and became the theater of the wars of foreign powers.

The small states that set themselves up as a power against a power a thousand and many times greater experienced the necessary fate of their fall, and beside a regret at it stands the feeling of the necessity and of the guilt that pygmies load upon themselves when, placing themselves beside colossi, they are trampled underfoot.

Even the existence of the larger Italian states, which had formed themselves by swallowing up a mass of smaller ones, vegetated on in this way without force and true independence, a ball in the plans of foreign powers; they kept themselves up a little longer through the prudence of humbling themselves skillfully and at the right time and through constant half-submissions holding off the full one, which however did not fail to come in the end.
zh: 意大利的各个部分把先前的国家瓦解掉、振作起来取得独立还没多久，就招来了更大强国的征服欲，成了外国列强打仗的舞台。
那些把自己当作一股力量、去和比它大上千倍万倍的力量对峙的小国，遭遇到自己覆灭的必然命运；在对它们的惋惜之外，还有那种对必然和罪责的感受——侏儒把自己摆到巨人旁边、被踩在脚下时，就把这加在自己身上。
那些通过吞掉大量小国而形成的较大的意大利国家，其存在也这样不死不活地延续着，没有力量，也没有真正的独立，在外国列强的谋划里只是一个球；它们能多维持一阵，靠的是精明——适时而巧妙地低头，靠不断半投降来挡开全投降，而全投降到末了还是没能躲过。

en: What has become of the multitude of the independent states Pisa, Siena, Arezzo, Ferrara, Milan, of these hundreds of states, as every city was one, what of the families of the many sovereign dukes, margraves, etc., of the princely houses Bentivoglio, Sforza, Gonzaga, Pico, Urbino, etc., and of the countless knightly nobility?

The independent states were swallowed by larger ones, and these again by larger ones, and so on; to one of the largest, Venice, a letter from a French general, delivered by an adjutant, has in our days given its end.
The most splendid princely houses no longer have sovereignty, nor any political, representative significance.
The noblest lineages have become court nobility.
zh: 比萨、锡耶纳、阿雷佐、费拉拉、米兰这一大堆独立国家，这几百个国家——当时每个城市就是一个——都成了什么；许多拥有主权的公爵、侯爵等等的家族，本蒂沃利奥、斯福尔扎、贡扎加、皮科、乌尔比诺这些王公世家，还有数不清的骑士贵族，又都成了什么？
独立国家被更大的国家吞掉，更大的又被更大的吞掉，如此下去；其中最强大的一个——威尼斯，在我们这个时代，一封由副官送来的法国将军的信就给它送了终。
最风光的王公世家既不再有主权，也不再有任何政治上的、代表制的意义。
最高贵的门第变成了宫廷贵族。

en: In the period of misfortune, when Italy hastened toward its misery and was the battlefield of the wars that foreign princes waged for its lands, at the same time supplied the means for those wars and was their prize, when it entrusted its own defence to assassination, poison and treachery or to bands of foreign rabble, which were always costly and devastating for their paymasters, and still more often terrible and dangerous, from whose leaders some raised themselves up to become princes, when Germans, Spaniards, French and Swiss plundered it and foreign cabinets decided the fate of this nation, - in the deep feeling of this condition of universal misery, of hatred, of ruin, of blindness, an Italian statesman with cold deliberation grasped the necessary idea of saving Italy by uniting it into one state.

He marked out with strict consistency the path that both this salvation and the corruption and blind frenzy of the time necessarily made necessary, and called upon his prince to take on the sublime role of a savior of Italy and the glory of putting an end to its misfortune, with the following words:
zh: 在那段不幸的时期，意大利正奔向自己的苦难，是外国君主为争夺它的土地而打仗的战场，同时又供给这些战争手段，又是这些战争的战利品；它把自己的防御交给暗杀、毒药和背叛，或者交给外来的流氓团伙，这些团伙对于出钱雇它们的主人总是费钱又毁坏地方，更常常是可怕而危险的，它们的头目里有些还爬上了君主的位子；当德意志人、西班牙人、法国人和瑞士人把它抢劫一空，外国内阁决定这个民族的命运时，——在这种普遍苦难、仇恨、瓦解和盲目的状况的深切感受中，一位意大利政治家以冷静的审慎抓住了那个必然的观念：把意大利联合成一个国家来拯救它。
他以严格的彻底性勾画出了这条道路，无论是这种拯救，还是时代的腐败和盲目的狂乱，都必然要求走上这条路；他用下面的话号召他的君主去承担意大利拯救者的崇高角色，去获得结束意大利不幸的荣耀：

en: 166) 'If, as has been said, it was necessary that, in order to see Moses' greatness, the people of Israel was a slave in Egypt, that, in order to recognize the sublimity and the courage of Cyrus, the Persians were oppressed by the Medes, and that, in order to bring the excellence of Theseus to light, the Athenians were split apart, so it was now, if one wants to see the greatness of spirit of an Italian, necessary that Italy fell into its present condition, that it be more enslaved than the Hebrews, more oppressed than the Persians, more split apart than the Athenians, without a head, without order, beaten, robbed, torn apart, plundered, and that it had to bear every kind of ruin.'

And although since then a trace has at times been perceived in someone that one could have thought he had been ordained by God for Italy's redemption, yet it has shown itself that afterwards, at the summit of his rise, he was cast off by fortune, so that Italy, left as it were lifeless, still waits for who it might be who heals its blows, puts an end to the devastations and plunderings of Lombardy and the embezzlements and extortions in the kingdom of Naples and in Tuscany, and lets Italy recover from the wounds that in the long time have already eaten into it ...
zh: 166）“正如已经说过的，如果为了看到摩西的伟大，以色列民族必须在埃及做奴隶，如果为了认识居鲁士的崇高和勇气，波斯人必须受米底人压迫，如果为了把忒修斯的卓越显扬出来，雅典人必须四分五裂，那么现在，如果人们想看到一个意大利人的精神伟大，意大利就必须陷入它目前的状况，必须比希伯来人更受奴役，比波斯人更受压迫，比雅典人更加四分五裂，没有首领，没有秩序，被打、被抢、被撕碎、被掠夺，必须承受各种各样的毁灭。
而尽管自那以后，人们有时在某人身上觉察到一点迹象，让人以为他是上帝指定来解救意大利的，结果还是表明，他随后在上升的顶峰上被幸运抛弃了；于是意大利像是被丢下、没了生气，至今还在等，等着那个能治好它创伤的人，等着那个终结伦巴第的荒废和抢掠、终结那不勒斯王国和托斯卡纳的侵吞和勒索、让意大利从长期已经咬进它身体里的伤口中痊愈的人……

en: Here there is complete justice, for that war is just because it is necessary, and those weapons are holy where no hope exists except through them ...
zh: 这里有完全的正义，因为那场战争是正义的，因为它是必要的；而那些武器是神圣的，因为在除了它们就没有希望的地方就是这样……

en: Everything has contributed to Your greatness, the rest remains for You to do.
God does not want to do everything, so as not to rob us of free will and of the part of the honor that is to fall to us ...
zh: 一切都为您的伟大出了力，剩下的还有待您去做。
上帝不愿把一切都做完，免得夺走我们的自由意志，也免得夺走那本该落到我们头上的那份荣耀……

en: And I cannot say with what love he [the liberator of Italy] would be received in all those provinces that have suffered from these inundations from abroad, with what thirst for revenge, with what unshakeable fidelity, with what reverence, with what tears.
Which doors would remain closed to him, which communities would refuse him obedience?
Where would envy oppose itself to him, which Italian would refuse him allegiance?' -
zh: 我也说不出，他〔意大利的解放者〕会在所有那些在外来的这些洪流下吃过苦的地方受到怎样的爱戴，带着怎样的复仇渴望，怀着怎样不可动摇的忠诚，怀着怎样的敬畏，流着怎样的眼泪。
哪扇门会对他关着，哪个市镇会拒绝听从他？
哪里会有嫉妒站出来跟他作对，哪个意大利人会拒绝跟随他？”——

en: One can perceive that a man who speaks with this truth of seriousness had neither baseness in his heart nor jesting in his head.
As for those principles, in general opinion the name Machiavelli already carries the seal of condemnation with it, and opinion has made Machiavellian and abominable principles synonymous.

The idea of a state that a people is to constitute has been drowned out for so long by a blind clamor of a so-called freedom that perhaps the whole misery that Germany [endured] in the Seven Years' War and in this last French war, and all further formation of reason and the experience with the French frenzy for freedom, are not sufficient to raise the truth that freedom is possible only in the lawful union of a people into a state to the belief of peoples or to a principle of a science of the state.
zh: 可以看出，一个带着这种严肃的真理说话的人，心里没有卑劣，头脑里也没有玩笑。
至于那些原则，在一般的看法里，马基雅维利这个名字本身就带着被唾弃的印记，而一般的看法已经把马基雅维利式的原则和可恶的原则当成一回事了。
一个民族应当构成一个国家，这个国家的观念被一种所谓自由的盲目叫喊压得太久，以致也许德意志在七年战争和这最近一场法国战争里〔遭受〕的全部苦难，还有理性的全部进一步教养和对法国自由狂热的经验，都不足以把这条真理抬升为各民族的信仰、或一门国家学的一条原则：自由只有在一个民族依法联合成为一个国家时才可能。

en: Even the purpose that Machiavelli sets before himself, of raising Italy into one state, is misjudged by the blindness that recognizes in Machiavelli's work nothing but a founding of tyranny, a golden mirror for an ambitious oppressor.
But even if it is granted, so [it is] said, the means are abominable, and there morality has wide scope to peddle its trivialities, that the end does not sanctify the means, and so forth.

But here there can be no question of any choice of means: gangrenous limbs cannot be healed with lavender water; a condition in which poison and assassination have become ordinary weapons tolerates no gentle counter-attempts.
A life close to decomposition can be reorganized only through the most violent procedure.
zh: 甚至马基雅维利预先设定的那个目的，即把意大利提升为一个国家，也被那种盲目错认了，这种盲目在马基雅维利的作品里看到的无非是一场暴政的建立、一面供野心勃勃的压迫者照影的金镜。
但就算这个目的被承认，据说手段也是可恶的，于是道德就有了广阔的余地，可以把它那些老生常谈——目的并不使手段神圣化等等——摆出来兜售。
但这里根本谈不上什么手段的选择：坏疽的肢体不能用薰衣草水治好；一个毒药、暗杀已成为寻常武器的状态，容不下温和的反击尝试。
临近腐烂的生命只能靠最暴烈的手段重新组织起来。

en: It is highly unreasonable to treat the execution of an idea that is drawn immediately from the intuition of the condition of Italy as an indifferent compendium of moral-political principles suited to all conditions, that is, therefore suited to no condition.

One must approach the reading of The Prince directly from the history of the centuries that elapsed before Machiavelli and the contemporaneous history of Italy, with the impression that these have given, and he will not [merely] be justified, but will appear as a most great and true conception of a genuine political head of the greatest and noblest mind.
zh: 把一种直接从意大利状况的直观中汲取出来的观念的实施，当作一部无所谓的、适用于一切状况、也就是说对任何状况都不适用的道德政治原则大全来处理，是极不理性的。
人们必须带着马基雅维利之前逝去的几个世纪的历史、同时代意大利的历史，以及这些历史留下的印象，直接去读《君主论》，这样他就不只是得到辩护，而会显现为一个真正的政治头脑所作的最伟大、最真实的构想，出自最伟大、最高尚的心智。

en: It would not be superfluous to say something about that which one usually overlooks, namely about the remaining truly ideal demands that Machiavelli makes on an excellent prince and which probably have been fulfilled since that time by no prince and not [even] by the one who refuted him.
But that which one calls the abominable means that Machiavelli is said to have advised must still be viewed from another point of view.

Italy was to be one state; this counted as a principle even then, when the emperor still counted as the supreme feudal lord - and this universal Machiavelli presupposes, this he demands, this is his principle against the misery of his country.
From here the procedure of the prince appears from a quite different side.
What, done by a private man against a private man or by one state against another or against a private man, would be abominable, is now just punishment.

Against a state, the bringing about of anarchy is the highest, or rather the only, crime; for all crimes that the state has to take up lead there, and those who attack not mediately, like other criminals, but immediately the state itself are the greatest criminals, and the state has no higher duty than to preserve itself and to destroy the power of these criminals in the surest way.

The exercise of this highest duty by the state is no longer a means, it is punishment, or if punishment itself were a means, then every punishment of any criminal would have to be called an abomination and every state would be in the position of using abominable means, death, long imprisonment, for the sake of its preservation.
zh: 说说人们通常忽略的那一点不会多余，也就是马基雅维利对一个卓越君主提出的其余那些真正理想的要求，而从那时起，大概没有任何君主满足过它们，连那个反驳他的人也没有。
但是人们所谓马基雅维利曾建议的那些可恶手段，还必须从另一个角度来考察。
意大利应当成为一个国家；这一点在当时仍被当作原则，那时皇帝仍被看作最高的封主——而这个普遍者正是马基雅维利所预设的，这是他要求的，这是他对付自己国家悲惨状况的原则。
从这里看，这位君主的做法就呈现出完全不同的另一面。
由私人对私人、或由一个国家对另一个国家、或对一个私人做出来会显得可恶的事，现在就是公正的惩罚。
对一个国家来说，制造无政府状态是最高的、或者不如说是唯一的罪行；因为国家所要处理的一切罪行都汇向那里，而那些不像别的罪犯那样间接地、而是直接攻击国家本身的人，就是最大的罪犯，国家也没有比保存自身、并以最可靠的方式摧毁这些罪犯的权力更高的义务。
国家对这项最高义务的行使不再是手段，它就是惩罚；或者，如果惩罚本身是一种手段，那么对任何一个罪犯的每一次惩罚都必须叫做可恶之举，而每个国家都会落入这样的境地：为了自己的保存而使用可恶的手段——死亡、长期监禁。

en: The Roman Cato the Younger has the privilege of being trotted out by every freedom-shrieker, and he was the greatest promoter [of the plan] that sole rule be transferred to Pompey, not out of friendship for Pompey, but because anarchy was the greater evil; and he killed himself, not because what the Romans at that time still called freedom, anarchy, had perished - for the party of Pompey, with whom he stood, was only a different party from that of Caesar - but out of stubbornness of character, which would not submit to his reviled and hated enemy - his death was a party matter.
zh: 罗马的小加图享有被每一个自由叫嚷者抬出来的特权，而他正是把独自统治的权力交给庞培这一[计划]的最大推动者，不是出于对庞培的友谊，而是因为无政府状态是更大的祸害；他自杀，也不是因为罗马人当时还称之为自由的东西、也就是无政府状态，已经覆灭——因为他所站的庞培那一党，不过是与凯撒不同的一党而已——而是出于性格的执拗，不肯向自己唾骂和憎恨的敌人屈服——他的死是一桩党争之事。

en: The one from whom Machiavelli had hoped for the salvation of Italy was, by all [reckoning], the Duke of Valentinois, a prince who, with the help of his uncle and through bravery as well as deceit of every kind, had formed a state out of the principalities of the dukes Ursino, Colonna, of Urbino, etc., and the domains of the Roman barons.

His memory and that of his uncle: - even if one wants to deduct all deeds imposed on them merely by bare rumors and the hatred of their enemies, their memory as men is branded before posterity, if it may presume to judge men morally, and the duke and his uncle, but not their work, have perished.
It is they who acquired for the Roman See a state whose existence Julius II well knew how to use and to make formidable and which endures to this day.
zh: 马基雅维利曾指望来拯救意大利的那个人，按一切[看法]就是瓦伦蒂诺公爵，这位君主靠他叔父的帮助，凭勇武以及各种各样的欺诈，从奥尔西尼、科隆纳、乌尔比诺等公爵的领地以及罗马男爵们的领地里拼凑出了一个国家。
他和他叔父的声名：——即使人们愿意把所有仅凭流言和他们敌人的仇恨被栽到他们头上的行为都扣除掉，他们作为人的声名在后世面前——如果后世竟敢对人作道德审判的话——也已经被打上烙印；而公爵和他叔父是毁掉了，但他们的作品没有。
正是他们为罗马教廷挣得了一个国家，尤利乌斯二世很懂得利用这个国家的存在，并把它变得令人生畏，而它一直存在到今天。

en: If Machiavelli attributes the fall of Cesare Borgia, besides political mistakes, also to the accident that threw him onto the sickbed precisely at the most decisive moment of Alexander's death, then we must on the contrary discern in his case more a higher necessity, which let him neither enjoy the fruits of his deeds nor develop them into greater power, because nature, as is shown by his vices, seems to have determined him more for an ephemeral splendor and for a mere instrument of the founding of a state, and because therefore of the power to which he raised himself a great part rested not on an inner and also not on an outer natural right, but was grafted onto the foreign branch of the spiritual dignity of his uncle.
zh: 如果说马基雅维利把切萨雷·博尔贾的失败除了政治上的失误之外也归给偶然，说那偶然恰在亚历山大去世的最关键时刻把他抛到了病床上，那么我们相反必须在他的遭遇中更多看到一种更高的必然性，这种必然性使他既不能享受自己行为的果实，也不能把那些果实发展成更大的权力，因为自然——从他的种种恶习可以看出——似乎更多把他规定为一时的光彩、规定为建立国家的一件纯粹工具，而且因为，在他奋力攀上的那种权力中，很大一部分并不基于某种内在的、也不基于某种外在的自然权利，而是嫁接在他叔父的教会尊位的异己枝条上的。

en: Machiavelli's work remains a great testimony that he delivered to his time and to his own belief that the fate of a people hastening toward its political downfall could be saved by genius.

Still remarkable in the misunderstanding of and hatred against Machiavelli's Prince, in the particular fate of this work, is that from a kind of instinct a future monarch, whose whole life and deeds have most clearly expressed the dissolution of the German state into independent states, made his school exercise on this Machiavelli and set against him moral chrias whose emptiness he himself showed both by his conduct and expressly in his literary works, in that he, e.g., in the preface to the History of the First Silesian War denies treaties between states their binding force when they are no longer in accordance with the best of a state.
zh: 马基雅维利的作品始终是一份伟大的见证，是他留给自己的时代、也留给他自己的信念的见证：一个奔向政治灭亡的民族的命运，可以靠天才来拯救。
在对马基雅维利《君主论》的误解和仇恨中，这部作品的特殊命运还有一点值得注意：出于某种本能，一位未来的君主——他的一生和行事最清楚地道出了德意志国家解体为各个独立国家这件事——竟拿这个马基雅维利来做自己的学校作业，对他摆出道德训诫文，而这些训诫文的空洞，他自己既用行动、也在他的著述中明确地表明过，比如他在《第一次西里西亚战争史》的序言里就说，各国之间的条约一旦不再符合某个国家的最善，就没有约束力。

en: But otherwise the more cunning public, which could not leave the genius in Machiavelli's works unnoticed and at the same time thought too morally to approve his principles, yet in good intent wanted to save him himself, has honestly and finely enough reconciled this contradiction in such a way that Machiavelli had not been in earnest about it, but that the whole was a fine persiflage, an irony, and one cannot help complimenting this public, which scents irony, on its subtlety.
zh: 不过除此之外，更狡猾的读者大众——他们无法对马基雅维利作品中的天才视而不见，同时又太讲道德，不肯认同他的原则，却出于善意仍想把他本人救出来——已经足够诚实而巧妙地把这个矛盾调和成这样：马基雅维利对此并不是认真的，整个东西只是一种精巧的戏仿、一种反讽；人不禁要对这种嗅出反讽的读者大众的精细奉上几句恭维。

en: Machiavelli's voice has died away without effect.
zh: 马基雅维利的声音没有产生任何效果，就消散了。

29.en: [9. The Politics of the Two German Great Powers]
29.zh: [9. 两个德意志大邦的政治]

en: 168) Germany shares with the former Italy the fate of having been for many centuries the scene of internal wars, but also the scene of the wars of foreign powers, of being plundered, robbed, insulted, despised by friends and usually diminished in peace.
In this fate it is much later than Italy.
Sweden is the actual first foreign power that has significantly rummaged in its entrails and helped shatter the preceding tottering system of connection.
From then on foreign powers decided Germany's lot.
It had already earlier ceased to be formidable to foreign lands.
From then on it ceased to settle its internal affairs independently for itself, to decide about itself; it has given its fate out of its hand.
zh: 168) 德意志和前意大利共有的命运是：许多世纪以来一直是内部战争的舞台，但也是外国势力战争的舞台，被朋友掠夺、抢劫、侮辱、轻视，并且通常在和平时期被削减。
在这种命运上，它比意大利晚得多。
瑞典是真正第一个在其内脏里大肆翻搅、并帮着打碎此前那套摇摇欲坠的联合体系的外国势力。
从那时起，外国势力就决定着德意志的命运。
它更早就已经不再让外国感到可怕了。
从那时起，它就不再独立地为自己料理内部事务、对自己作出决定；它已经把自己的命运交出了手。

en: But Germany's fate differs essentially from the fate of Italy in this, that the states into which Italy had fallen apart were, through the condition of the world in general, still for a long time capable of holding their own even against much greater powers, or that the disproportionate extent had not made their power equally disproportionate; but just as Greece was capable not only of resisting the Persians but of defeating them, so in earlier times a city like Milan was able to defy Frederick's power and to hold itself against it, and still later Venice held out against the League of Cambrai.

But a possibility that small states withstand great ones has now completely vanished; and the sovereignty of the states of Germany has formed itself more at a time when this possibility was no longer present.

The states of Germany have therefore passed not from union into a complete separation, but immediately again into unions of another kind; the mass has not fallen apart into many pieces and thus remained fragmented for a time, but in the mass new cores have formed, around which the parts that tore themselves loose from the whole gathered into new masses.
zh: 但德意志的命运与意大利的命运有一个本质的区别：意大利所分裂成的那些国家，靠当时世界的一般状况，在很长一段时间里还有能力抵挡强大得多的列强，或者说，那种不相称的幅员并没有使它们的力量也变得同样不相称；而是像希腊有能力不仅抵抗波斯人、而且战胜他们一样，在较早的时代，一个像米兰这样的城市就能顶住弗里德里希的势力，并在它面前保住自己，再晚一些，威尼斯也顶住了康布雷同盟。
但小国抵抗大国的这种可能性，如今已经彻底消失了；而德意志各邦的主权，多半是在这种可能性已经不再存在的时代才形成起来的。
因此，德意志的各邦并不是从结合走向完全的分裂，而是立刻又转入另一种结合；这一大团并没有碎成许多块，并就这样碎裂着过了一段时间，而是在这一大团里形成了新的核心，那些从整体上挣脱下来的部分，就围绕这些新核心聚成新的大团。

en: Religion and independence as states were formerly the interests around which, as around centers, the German estates gathered; both centers formed their political system.
But these centers have disappeared.

Religion has not only been preserved, but the spirit of the times has placed it beyond all danger; likewise the estates have put themselves in possession of independence, but alongside the Austrian power, against which anxieties were formerly directed under the name of a universal monarchy, the Prussian monarchy has formed itself, which, strong enough for itself, in the Seven Years' War held out not only against the power of the Austrian but of several monarchies, and since then has enlarged itself still further in Poland and in Franconia.
zh: 宗教和作为国家的独立性，从前就是那些利益，德意志各等级围绕着它们、把它们当作中心聚集起来；这两个中心各自形成了自己的政治体系。
但这两个中心已经消失了。
宗教不仅被保存下来了，而且时代的精神已经把它置于一切危险之上；同样，各等级也使自己取得了独立，但在奥地利势力旁边——从前人们的忧虑正是以普遍君主制之名针对这股势力的——又形成了普鲁士君主国，它凭自身已经足够强大，在七年战争中不仅顶住了奥地利君主国的势力，还顶住了好几个君主国的势力，此后又在波兰和弗兰肯进一步扩大了自己。

en: Through this its power Prussia has stepped outside the sphere of the common interest in the preservation of its independence, and is therefore no longer to be regarded as the natural center for the estates for the preservation of independence.
It can desire the alliance of other estates, it is in this independent of the assistance of the German princes, it can protect itself on its own.
The league of the German estates with it is therefore unequal, for it needs the same less than they need it, and the advantage must therefore also be unequal.
Prussia can itself awaken anxieties.
zh: 普鲁士凭它这种势力，已经走到了以保持自己的独立为内容的共同利益的范围之外，因此不再能看作各等级为保持独立而依靠的那个自然中心。
它可以希望别的等级同它结盟，在这件事上它不依赖德意志各诸侯的援助，它能靠自己保护自己。
德意志各等级与它的联合因此是不对等的，因为它对这一联合的需要比它们对这一联合的需要要少，所以好处也必然不对等。
普鲁士自己也可能引起忧虑。

en: In the last war four political systems have shown themselves in Germany: the one the Austrian, the other the imperial, [the third] the neutral, the fourth the Prussian.
zh: 在最近这场战争中，德意志出现了四种政治体系：一种是奥地利的，另一种是皇帝的，〔第三种〕是中立的，第四种是普鲁士的。

en: Austria has had no immediate assistance, [except] perhaps from a few small princes, [for example] the Bishop of Brixen, who lies in the middle of its states.

As imperial house it demands of the German estates assistance and common cooperation; and belonging to the imperial system, all the less powerful estates have held to it, especially those of southern Germany, which can preserve any independence only through the continued existence of a German Empire, chiefly ecclesiastical estates and imperial cities.
zh: 奥地利没有得到直接的援助，〔除非〕也许来自几个小诸侯，〔例如〕布里克森的主教，他的地盘就在奥地利各邦的中间。
它作为皇室，向德意志各等级要求援助和共同的协助；而所有势力较小的等级，尤其是德意志南部的那些等级，都归附于皇帝的体系，因为它们只有靠一个德意志帝国继续存在，才能保有一点独立性，其中首先是教会等级和帝国城市。

en: The third system is chiefly the system of Bavaria, Baden and Saxony, which - neither in political connection with Austria nor Prussia nor the Empire - acted according to their particular interest with regard to war or peace or neutrality.
zh: 第三种体系主要是巴伐利亚、巴登和萨克森的体系，它们——既不同奥地利、也不同普鲁士、也不同帝国处于政治上的联系之中——在战争、和平还是中立的问题上，都按自己的特殊利益行事。

en: The fourth system comprises the estates of northern Germany, which, under Prussia's mediation, concluded a neutrality treaty with France and placed themselves under Prussia's protection, which has taken over the guarantee of the tranquillity of northern Germany.
zh: 第四种体系包括德意志北部的各等级，它们在普鲁士的中介下与法国缔结了一项中立条约，把自己置于普鲁士的保护之下，而普鲁士承担了保证德意志北部安宁的责任。

en: After Prussia had concluded peace with France, several northern states joined this peace treaty, and in the terror at the French success of arms in the campaign of 94, more than half of Germany combined in this neutrality.

When in the year 96 the French pressed as far as Bavaria, the city of Nuremberg wanted not merely to join this neutrality, but to make itself entirely into a Prussian country town, and it was occupied by Prussian troops, after a few years earlier Prussia had declared a part of its territory to belong to it on account of old claims and had taken the same into its power, just as it also abolished the immediacy of many imperial knights in Franconia, and from the German Empire Nuremberg for that reason, as well as the knighthood, could obtain no help.
zh: 普鲁士同法国缔结和约之后，好几个北方邦国加入了这项和约，而在对法国在 94 年战局中的军事胜利的惊恐中，德意志有一半以上联合起来加入了这一中立。
当 96 年法国人一直推进到巴伐利亚时，纽伦堡市不仅想加入这一中立，而且想干脆把自己变成一座普鲁士的外省城市，于是它被普鲁士军队占领了；而在此前几年，普鲁士就以旧有的权利要求为理由，宣布它的一部分领地属于自己，并把这部分领地拿到手中，同样也取消了弗兰肯许多帝国骑士的帝国直属地位，因此纽伦堡以及骑士阶层都没能从德意志帝国那里得到援助。

en: The estates of northern Germany have not themselves taken over the guarantee of their neutrality in the form of the otherwise usual circle associations, and Prussia is not one of the members of this union, but the head and the guarantor, and the estates contribute to the costs of the demarcation corps.

But no permanent federal council is assembled; rather it assembled only at certain times, in order to deliberate and decide about the regulation and continuation of this measure and of the cost contributions.
zh: 德意志北部的各等级并没有自己以通常那种帝国行政区联合的形式，来承担对自己中立的保证，而普鲁士不是这个联合体中的一员，而是它的首领和保证人，各等级则分担划界军团的费用。
但并没有一个常设的联盟议会开会，它只是在某些时候才聚会，为的是商议并决定这一措施和费用分摊的调整与继续。

en: But the true political relation of the estates came precisely to light when, at the end of the year 1800, the estates that were not assembled were minded to hold a new assembly - so this meeting and deliberation was refused them by Prussia, because Prussia as guarantor of the tranquillity of the North had to judge which measures were to be taken for this.
zh: 但各等级真正的政治关系恰好清楚地显露出来：当 1800 年年末，那些没有参加集会的等级打算举行一次新的集会时，——于是普鲁士拒绝了它们这次聚会和商议，因为普鲁士作为北方安宁的保证人，得由它来判断为此应当采取哪些措施。

en: When the northern coalition seemed about to fall into war with England over England's pretensions regarding neutral ships, Hanover, one of the main members of the league, whose neutrality was guaranteed to it, was (along with other imperial cities) occupied by Prussia.170) It had to dismiss its troops and take over the provisioning of the Prussian corps.
The peace has been ratified by the estates of the German Empire, yet Prussia has had its ratification officially announced for itself directly in Paris.
zh: 当北方同盟因为英国对中立船只的要求而似乎要同英国陷入战争时，汉诺威——这个同盟的主要成员之一，它的中立本来是得到保证的——（连同其他帝国城市一起）被普鲁士占领了。170) 它不得不遣散自己的军队，并承担普鲁士军团的给养。
和约已经由德意志帝国的各等级批准，但普鲁士却让它自己的批准直接正式在巴黎作了通告。

en: The whole history of the war, the separation of northern Germany from southern, the particular neutrality and peace acts of the former, while the latter languished under the most cruel misery and thus saw itself wholly abandoned by that former - make it clear not only that Germany is divided into independent states, but also that their interest is completely separated, and if the state bond is loose as in the Middle Ages, then no free union is to be expected after all.

With the most powerful of all interests, when Germany was diminished by the lands of the left bank of the Rhine, when the one half was flooded and plundered by the enemies, not only was no help in accordance with the imperial league rendered, but no voluntary help either.

The other estates had separated themselves from all cooperation, and one part, even by the fact that it placed its neutrality in the guarantee of a prince who was at the same time foreign, had at the same time given out of its hands the right of cooperation, to join in the general cooperation again, even the ability to deliberate about this with the fellow estates.
zh: 战争的全部历史，德意志北部与南部的分离，前者那些特别的中立和和约文件——当后者在最残酷的苦难中煎熬、因而看到自己完全被前者抛弃的时候——都清楚表明：不仅德意志已经分裂为一些独立的国家，而且它们的利益也完全分开了，而如果说国家纽带像中世纪那样松弛，那么毕竟不能指望会有什么自由的联合。
在一切利益中最重大的利益上，当德意志被削去了莱茵河左岸的那些地方，当它的一半被敌人淹没和洗劫时，人们不仅没有提供符合帝国同盟的援助，连自愿的援助也没有提供。
其他各等级已经把自己同一切共同行动分开了，而其中一部分甚至由于把自己的中立交托给一个同时是外邦君主的君主的保证，同时也把共同行动的权利交出了手，即重新加入共同行动的权利，甚至也交出了同与它同级的各方就此进行商议的能力。

en: Sweden did indeed publicly offer, at the resumption of the war, to provide its contingent.
But it has been reported that Prussia was unwilling to permit the passage through the neutrality line.

By the fact that Brandenburg not only in this war separated its interest completely from the interest of the German Empire and induced other estates likewise to separate theirs, and then placed them in the position of being able to compel them as guarantor, legally and through its power, to keep themselves separate, that it took from the Franconian knighthood its immediacy and from the imperial city of Nuremberg a part of its territory, and at the moment of distress accepted the complete surrender of the magistracy for occupation, afterwards occupied Hanover, which was in alliance with it on account of the tranquillity and security of northern Germany, disarmed it and burdened it with the requisition of provisions — through all these circumstances it has become clear what had long been present, that Prussia is to be regarded not as a German imperial prince on an equal footing with the other estates, but as a separate, sovereign, powerful state, not as an estate that would be capable of accepting equal conditions with other estates in an association.
zh: 战争重新开始时，瑞典虽然公开表示愿意派出它那份兵员。
但据传，普鲁士不肯允许它穿过中立线。

由于勃兰登堡不仅在这场战争中把自己的利益完全同德意志帝国的利益分隔开来，还促使别的等级也把各自的利益分隔开来，接着又使它们落到这样的境地：它作为保证人能从法理上并凭借自己的强力迫使它们保持分隔状态；由于它夺去了弗兰肯骑士阶层的帝国直属地位，又夺去帝国城市纽伦堡的一部分领地，并在危难时刻接受其市政机构完全交出、任由占领；后来还占领了因北德意志的安宁与安全而同它结盟的汉诺威，解除了它的武装，并对它课以给养的征用——正是通过这一切情形，早就存在着的东西才变得清楚：普鲁士不能看作一个与其他等级处于同等地位的德意志帝国诸侯，而应看作一个独立的、拥有主权的、强大的国家，不能看成一个在联合中有能力与其他等级接受同等条件的等级。

en: On the whole, through the last [war] more truth has come into the relations of states.

Insofar as states stand in a relation of power to one another, the illusions about this have vanished, and this relation has everywhere revealed itself, has been asserted, and the weaker states have been brought to the insight that they cannot put themselves on a level with the greater ones.

If a Republic of Geneva behaved as a sovereign state and boasted of being the first — εὔχετο — to send an envoy to the French Republic and to recognise it formally, then the relation of Geneva to France, when it was taken seriously, was soon determined otherwise; by contrast, to the Republic of San Marino Bonaparte made a present of a couple of cannons, because there was no relation there from which seriousness was to be made, other than that of an occasion to fill one's mouth with the name of a respect for republics.
zh: 总的说来，通过最近这场〔战争〕，各国关系中多了些真相。
既然各国彼此处在一种力量的关系中，关于这一点的种种错觉就消失了，这种关系到处都显露出来、得到主张，较弱的国家也被带到了这样的认识：它们不能把自己同较大的国家等量齐观。
如果一个日内瓦共和国以主权国家自居，还夸口说自己是第一个——εὔχετο——向法兰西共和国派出使节并正式承认它的，那么日内瓦同法国的关系一旦被当真，很快就被另行确定了；相反，圣马力诺共和国却得到波拿巴赠送的两门炮，因为那里并没有什么关系可以拿来当真，只不过有个由头，让人满口是尊重共和国的名号。

en: The Republic of Geneva has vanished, whereas to the Batavian, Helvetic, Cisalpine and Ligurian republics their independence and tranquillity and, if one will, neutrality is guaranteed with a strong garrison.
zh: 日内瓦共和国消失了，相反，巴达维亚、赫尔维蒂、内阿尔卑斯、利古里亚这几个共和国，它们的独立与安宁、如果人们愿意的话还有中立，都是用一支强大的驻军来保证的。

en: Such are the relations that more powerful states tie with weaker states according to the true difference of their strength.
zh: 较强大的国家依照彼此力量的真实差别同较弱的国家结成的，就是这样的关系。

en: Austria's relations with Germany date from old times, and they would have to turn out quite differently if Austria laid down the imperial crown and then, now entirely as a great sovereign power, entered with its neighbours into treaties of protection and guarantee, especially if it let it come to times of distress; in this advantage Austria stands far behind, [namely] that Austria's relations are old, whereas Brandenburg in peacetime need not enter into any determinate relations, but in wartime can make conditions for those who are in distress and weak and turn to it.

Since nowadays everything is to be calculated, the conditions can be made 10 % lower than those one fears from the enemy, or, because the enemy is altogether something so indeterminate and one fears everything from it, every determinate condition seems lower than the indeterminate one that is to be feared.
There, after all, one knows the extent of one's loss, and this is already a great reassurance.
zh: 奥地利同德意志的关系是从旧时代传下来的，如果奥地利放下皇冠，此后完全作为一个伟大的主权国家同它的邻邦订立保护和保证条约，这些关系就必定会完全是另一个样子，尤其是如果它任由事情拖到危难时期的话；在这个好处上奥地利差得远：奥地利的关系是旧的，而勃兰登堡在和平时期无须结成任何确定的关系，到了战争时期却可以向那些身处危难、力量薄弱而求助于它的人提出条件。
既然如今什么都要计算，条件就可以定得比人们所惧怕的敌人低 10 %，或者，因为敌人根本就是那么一种不确定的东西，人们又什么都怕它，于是任何确定的条件看起来都比那个不确定的、要怕的东西轻。
可那里的人毕竟知道自己损失的范围，这已经是一种很大的安慰了。

en: Formerly it was the popular opinion in the regions of the Rhine that, since of one state one part stood within the demarcation line and the other outside it under public and private contributions of the French, [when] now the provincial estates of both parts were to come together for the joint settling of the debts, the part that stood under French rule refused parity and equal participation, because it believed it would lose; this popular opinion may be unfounded, yet one always sees the judgment of the people from it in general.
zh: 从前在莱茵地区有一种民众看法：既然同一个国家的一部分处在分界线以内，另一部分处在分界线以外、受着法国人的公、私摊派，那么当两部分的地方等级要聚到一起共同清理债务时，处在法国统治下的那一部分就拒绝平等地位和平等的参与，因为它认为自己会吃亏；这种民众看法也许是没有根据的，但人们总还是能从中大体上看出民众的判断。

en: [Brandenburg thus has the advantage that it]171) either has the more powerful ones as friends or, because it otherwise stands in no relations of alliance and protection, treats them as enemies, and can also, in the case of a treaty of guarantee, annul it at once, because it is only something determinate and particular like every political treaty, and according to the essence of political treaties its annulment is not faithlessness, which this war has taught most of all, in which so many treaties have been annulled, tied again and annulled again.

Austria's connections with the estates, by contrast, seem [not] to be of the rank of ordinary political treaties; rather, if it placed itself in an ordinary relation toward an imperial estate, as Prussia can, then all the estates feel themselves attacked in this.
In the case of Prussia it seems natural, just as well as in the case of France etc.
zh: 〔所以勃兰登堡有这样的好处：它〕171) 要么把较强大的国家当作朋友，要么——因为它在别的方面不处在任何结盟和保护的关系中——把它们当敌人来对待，而且即使有保证条约，它也能立刻把条约废掉，因为这跟任何政治条约一样，只是某种确定的、单个的东西，而按照政治条约的本质，废掉它并不算背信弃义，这一点这场战争教得最清楚，其间那么多条约被废掉、重新缔结、又再废掉。
相反，奥地利同各等级的联系似乎〔不〕属于通常政治条约的档次；可是一旦它像普鲁士那样，把自己摆到与某个帝国等级相对的通常关系中，所有等级就都觉得自身在其中受到了侵犯。
在普鲁士那里，这似乎是自然的，就像在法国等等那里一样。

en: Through its power and through the appearance of the same in the cases cited above, Prussia has stepped out of the same rank with the other estates.

The pure interest of their political independence they can find only in themselves, and in this respect an association of them, a true league of estates, is conceivable; but also only conceivable, for on the one hand the estates among themselves are again so unequal in power that they are capable of no true equal union.
zh: 凭借自己的强力，并凭借这种强力在上述那些情况中的显现，普鲁士已经走出了与其他等级平列的行列。
他们纯粹的政治独立利益，只能在自己身上找到，就这一点而言，他们的一种联合、一个真正的等级同盟，是可以设想的；但也只是可以设想而已，因为一方面各等级彼此之间在力量上又如此不平等，以致他们根本不能结成任何真正平等的联合。

en: An abbey, an imperial city, an immediate nobleman can far less fear to become the object of the Austrian monarchy's greed for aggrandizement than [of] a less great power.

Prussian power, although it is a great monarchy, stands in regard to this capacity to give small estates anxieties, and to the use of small advantages, more on the line of lesser estates, because, like France's, its statecraft is entirely calculating, its military power was disproportionate to its extent and therefore had to seek the sum of small advantages — just as the French Republic acted throughout according to general principles, pursued them with its power into the smallest details and suppressed all particular rights and relations under these principles — and one could say, because its new politics has emerged not from a royal, majestic principle but from the bourgeois character, and behaves, e.g., toward the Austrian power in the relation of a citizen who by his work has laboriously acquired his treasures from the penny upward, toward the free nobleman rich from forebears, whose possession rests on his soil and remains the same even if in small things he lets his household servants or neighbours have their way.
Its wealth is not a sum — but the sum is diminished by the taking away of individual items — but something abiding, unchangeable.
zh: 一座修道院、一个帝国城市、一个帝国直属的贵族，害怕自己成为奥地利君主国扩张欲的对象，要比害怕自己成为某个不那么大的强权的对象少得多。

普鲁士的强力尽管是一个庞大的君主国，在使小等级产生忧虑的这种能力上、在利用小便宜上，却更与那些不那么大的等级处在一条线上，因为跟法国的治国术一样，它的治国术完全是精打细算的，它的军事力量同它的幅员根本不成比例，因此不得不去寻求小便宜的总和——正如法兰西共和国完全按普遍原则行事，用它的力量一路追究到最细小的细节，把所有特殊的权利和关系都压制在这些原则之下——也可以说，因为它的新政治不是从国王的、君主的原理中产生，而是从市民性中产生出来的，例如它面对奥地利这个强权时，就处在这样一个关系中：一个靠自己的劳作从一文钱起辛苦积攒起财富的市民，面对一个祖上就富有、自由的贵族，后者的产业稳稳立在自己的土地上，即使他在小事上让自家的仆役或邻人占些便宜，这产业也还是原样。
它的财富不是一个总和——而总和会因为拿走个别的东西而减少——而是一种持存的、不变的东西。

en: The small estates, which must have the greatest anxieties about their independence, can attach themselves with confidence only to a power whose politics and magnanimity are at once capable and inclined to protect their existence, and one has also always seen the ecclesiastical princes, abbots and imperial cities attach themselves to the emperor and most faithfully observe their obligations toward him and the German Empire.
zh: 那些必定最担心自身独立的小等级，只能满怀信任地去依附这样一个强权：它的政治和宽厚既有能力、也愿意保护他们的存在；人们也一直看到，教会诸侯、修道院长、帝国城市总是依附皇帝，并且对皇帝和德意志帝国最忠实地尽自己的义务。

en: Even if the more powerful imperial estates wanted to unite among themselves and invented a way that such a coalition would not have the fate of all coalitions, even if the union of their troops formed a power that could withstand a great power, they would still never come into the position of having anxieties about only one power — for this one power would necessarily have to fear the participation of other powers against it; but against the agreement of several powers a union would be able to do nothing, both because of its lesser military power and because of its scattered geographical situation.
This situation has formed itself according to a plan, like the extent of great empires.
It is in military regard in itself thoroughly weak, and because the union would be something new, these states would also not be rich enough to gird themselves with rows of fortresses.
zh: 即使较强大的帝国等级彼此联合起来，并且想出一种办法，使这样一种同盟不至于落得一切同盟的下场，即使它们兵力的联合形成一种能够抵抗某个大强权的力量，它们也永远不会落到只需担心一个强权的地步——因为这个强权必然要担心别的强权站到对面去；而面对好几个强权的一致，一个联合则既由于它较弱的军力、又由于它分散的地理位置，什么也做不了。
这种位置是依照一种计划形成的，就像大帝国的幅员一样。
从军事上看，它本身就完全薄弱，而且因为这种联合是件新事，这些国家也不会富到能用一排排要塞把自己围起来。

en: Their politics must, according to circumstances, attach them now to this, now to that greater power, and their fate must be the common fate of a weaker ally or of a weak enemy.
zh: 他们的政治必定依情况时而使他们依附这个、时而依附那个较大的强权，而他们的命运也就是一个较弱盟友或一个弱小敌人的平常命运。

en: The fate of the German estates stands immediately between the politics of two great powers.

Both are now alike in this, that their relation to Germany is chiefly a political one, and [indeed] Prussia's relation even more than Austria's, because this power at the same time bears the imperial crown and is thereby, from old times on, restricted by the weight of infinitely many rights.
zh: 德意志各等级的命运，直接就夹在两个大国的政治之间。
两者如今在这一点上是相同的：它们与德意志的关系主要是一种政治关系，而且[确实]普鲁士的关系还更甚于奥地利的关系，因为这个大国同时戴着皇冠，并因此从旧时起就受到无穷多的权利之重量的限制。

en: The remaining interests, in which the powers were at variance, have evened out.

Through the diversity of these interests Prussia became great, in that it attached itself to those opposed to the House of Austria or placed itself at their head; but time by itself has partly done away with the separation of the interest of a great part of Germany from the Austrian interest, partly separated Prussia's interest from the interest of the German estates.
zh: 其余那些使各强国彼此不同的利益，已经互相拉平了。
正是通过这些利益的不同，普鲁士才变得强大，因为它投靠了与奥地利王室相反的那些利益，或者站到了它们的前列；但时间本身却一方面消除了德意志很大一部分的利益同奥地利利益的分离，另一方面又把普鲁士的利益同德意志各等级的利益分开了。

en: One chief interest, at the head of whose defense [Prussia] appeared, was religion.
zh: 有一个主要的利益——[普鲁士]曾站在捍卫它的最前面——就是宗教。

en: The German estates themselves, in older times chiefly Saxony and Hesse, and foreign powers, Sweden and France, had formerly championed this interest against the emperor, and Prussia at that time played no role, or as Brandenburg only a subordinate one.
In the Seven Years' War this interest came to light not so much on the side of the powers against one another as in the opinion of the people, and it did not fail of its effect.

There always remained a kind of mistrust, and if the Protestants did not see themselves as such attacked, they still always feared the possibility; they still credited the House of Austria with the will, the height of bigotry and an influence of the new, yielding pope, of the Jesuits, of priests in general, so far as it would be capable of that, and they saw in Prussia the guarantor and, if the emergency really came, the savior of their freedom of faith and conscience.
zh: 德意志各等级本身——在较早的时代主要是萨克森和黑森——以及外国势力，即瑞典和法国，从前都曾为这个利益而对抗皇帝，而普鲁士当时还没有扮演任何角色，或者作为勃兰登堡只扮演了一个从属的角色。
在七年战争中，这个利益与其说是从各强国彼此对立的那一面、不如说是从民众舆论中显露出来，而它的作用并没有落空。
总还留着一种不信任，而新教徒即使没有看到自己作为新教徒受到攻击，也仍旧一直害怕那种可能性；他们仍旧认为奥地利王室有那种意志、有那种偏执的高度，也有那个新的、肯让步的教皇、耶稣会士、总之教士们的影响，只要它有能力这样做；他们在普鲁士身上看到的则是他们信仰自由和良心自由的保证人，并且一旦危急现实地来临，还是他们的拯救者。

en: The petty and, according to its aim, fanatical politics of the Jesuits has long since ceased to be the politics of the courts.
Especially since Joseph II.'s
times this anxiety has disappeared from the Protestants.

Joseph II.'s procedure was not merely the idea of a single monarch, which can die out again with his death172), but his successors have both preserved precisely these principles, and they have also passed over generally into the firm, universal mass of education and state principles.
zh: 耶稣会士那种琐屑的、就其目的而言狂热的政策，早已不再是宫廷的政策了。
特别是自约瑟夫二世
的时代以来，这种忧虑在新教徒那里已经消失了。
约瑟夫二世的做法并不只是一个单个君主的念头——这种念头可以随着他的死而重新灭绝172)——而是他的继承者们既保留了这些原则，它们也一般地进入了教养和国家原则的那种牢固而普遍的总体之中。

en: Also that which even later was especially an object of the interest of the Protestant part of the imperial princes, the circumstances of the Protestants in the Palatinate, the only remnant contradicting the principles of our time, is now removed.

The spirit of the times, the way of proceeding of governments that has become firm and turned into principles, has astonishingly diminished the importance of the corpus evangelicorum and thereby also of the chief head.
zh: 还有那个甚至到后来仍特别成为帝国诸侯中新教一方利益之对象的东西，即普法尔茨新教徒的处境——这是唯一与我们时代的原则相矛盾的残余——如今也已经被清除了。
时代的精神，即各国政府那种已经固定下来并变成原则的做法，已经惊人地削弱了 corpus evangelicorum 的重要性，从而也削弱了它的首领的重要性。

en: The craving of the Catholic estates to procure supremacy for the Catholic religion has fallen away, and with it also the crooked means that one formerly used to move German imperial princes to convert to the Catholic religion, and which aroused so astonishingly much fear and anxiety in the Protestants.

The Catholic side no longer lays any value on it, because the state has already known in itself how to separate itself from the church, and experience has also shown that such means produced more the bad effect of mistrust and the increase of obstinacy than real benefit.
Soon, with regard to religion, the person of the prince has been separated from the land.

Even if the prince became Catholic, the relation of the land to the imperial diet remained Protestant, indeed the prince on his conversion to the Catholic religion lost power in his Protestant land, not only because of the mistrust in general that arose through it, but the influence that a Protestant prince has over the church system of his land was taken from him through reversals and the like, and he is placed in the relation of the Catholic prince of a Catholic land, in which the church is wholly independent of the secular power as regards its goods, the filling of offices and other arrangements, whereas the Protestant prince of a Protestant land is head and bishop at the same time.
Also, Catholic princely houses have in more recent times again [become Protestant].
zh: 天主教各等级要让天主教宗教取得至高权力的那种贪求已经消失，随之也消失了那些不正当的手段——人们从前曾用它们来促使德意志的帝国诸侯改宗天主教，而它们在新教徒那里引起的恐惧和忧虑又是那么惊人地多。
天主教一方已经不再看重这一点，因为国家本身早就懂得把自己同教会分开，而且经验也表明，这类手段带来的更多是不信任和更加固执的坏效果，而不是现实的好处。
不久，就宗教方面而言，君主的个人已经同领地分开了。

即使君主成了天主教徒，领地同帝国议会的关系也仍旧是新教的，甚至君主在改宗天主教时还在他的新教领地里失去了权力，这不仅是因为由此产生的那种普遍的不信任，而且一个新教君主对他的领地的教会事务具有的那种影响，也通过保证书之类的东西被从他那里拿走了，他被置于一个天主教领地的天主教君主的那种关系里——在那里，教会对自己的财产、职位的任命和其他安排完全独立于世俗权力，而一个新教领地的新教君主却同时是首领和主教。
此外，一些天主教诸侯家族在较近的时代又[成了新教的]。

en: Because such means fall away on the Catholic side, the Jesuit order has been abolished, tolerance has been introduced in the Catholic lands themselves, and civil rights have been granted to the Protestants contrary to the narrow-minded arrangements of the Peace of Westphalia, the long lists that teachers of constitutional law [gave] of the conversion of Protestant princes to the Catholic religion, the exposition of the malice of the Jesuits, the depiction of the oppression and hardships of the Protestants in Catholic [lands] have become historical objects of past things and no longer bugbears for the present.
zh: 由于这类手段从天主教一方消失了，耶稣会教团被解散了，在天主教国家本身也实行了宽容，并且不顾《威斯特伐利亚和约》那些心胸狭窄的规定而给予了新教徒市民权利，所以国家法教师们[所给出]的那些关于新教诸侯改宗天主教的长长的清单、对耶稣会士阴险手法的剖析、对天主教[国家]里新教徒所受压迫和困苦的描述，都成了过去之事的历史对象，而不再是吓唬当下的怪物。

en: Through the power of foreign assistance the Protestants have been freed for longer from the fear of seeing their faith suppressed by force, as they after all have never thirsted much for the martyr's crown.

And that proselytizing is no longer a system of a court has also partly freed them from the former hellish fear, that this faith of theirs might be taken from them by cunning and their conscience secretly played out of their pocket.
The length of time alone has already given them more confidence and security as to the possession of the truth.

It has long since ceased to be heard of that the Catholic confessor was regarded by the imperial diet as a puissance and that on the part of the imperial diet [a] request could have gone out to the emperor about this.
zh: 由于外来援助的力量，新教徒较长久地摆脱了眼看自己的信仰被暴力压制的恐惧，而他们本来也从未怎么渴慕过殉道者的冠冕。
而劝人改宗不再是一个宫廷的制度，这也部分地使他们摆脱了从前那种地狱般的恐惧，即唯恐他们这种信仰会被诡计夺走，良心会被人偷偷地从口袋里掏走。
单是时间的长久，就已经给了他们更多对拥有真理的信心和把握。
早就再也听不到这样的事了：天主教的忏悔神父被帝国议会看作一种 puissance，而帝国议会方面可以就此事向皇帝提出[一项]请求。

en: If Berlin private writers have wanted to awaken again this hellish fear among the Protestants through the frightful noise of Jesuit-sniffing, then such a thing is not only no longer a cabinet matter, no object of imperial diet deliberations, but appears merely as a silliness or otherwise an outbreak of a most limited interest, of discord among the branches of the Masonic order.
zh: 如果柏林的私人写作者想通过那种嗅寻耶稣会士的可怕喧嚷，重新在新教徒中间唤起这种地狱般的恐惧，那么这种事就不只是再也不是内阁事务、不是帝国议会商讨的对象，而只显得是一种无聊之举，或者是某种极其狭隘的利益的一次发作，即共济会各支派之间的不和。

en: Another interest was the rescue of that which one formerly called German freedom, against that which one called a universal monarchy or afterwards also the oriental system.
zh: 另一种利益，是保住人们从前称为德意志自由的那个东西，以对抗人们称为普遍君主制、或后来也称为东方体系的那个东西。

en: Since for ten years all Europe has fixed its attention on the fearful struggle of a people for freedom, and all Europe was in general movement on that account, it cannot be otherwise than that the concepts of freedom have undergone a change and have purified themselves out of their previous emptiness and indeterminacy.

German freedom formerly meant nothing other than the independence of the estates from the emperor, [that meant:] either slavery and despotism - or the abolition of the state union; the older times knew nothing third.
zh: 由于十年来整个欧洲都把注意力紧紧放在一个民族为自由而进行的可怕搏斗上，整个欧洲也因此处于普遍的动荡之中，所以事情不可能不是这样：关于自由的概念经历了一种变化，并从它们先前那种空洞和不确定中澄清了出来。
德意志自由从前无非是指各等级对皇帝的独立，〔这就是说：〕要么是奴役和专制——要么是废除国家联合；更早的时代不知道还有第三种。

en: Since Charles V the Spanish and the Austrian monarchy are no longer united, and for a century both have been possessed by quite different families.

Austria has lost great provinces, France and England have raised themselves to an equal greatness of power, Prussia and Russia have formed themselves; Austria is long since no longer the monarchy that would have no equal in Europe.

A system of the European balance has formed itself, i.e. a system by virtue of which usually all the powers of Europe take an interest in a war and every power is prevented from harvesting the fruits even of the most fortunate war, whether alone or even [only] in proportion to the advantages it has won.
Wars have already in themselves so much changed their nature that the conquest of a couple of islands or of a province costs many years of exertions, enormous sums, etc.
zh: 自查理五世以来，西班牙君主国和奥地利君主国就不再联合在一起了，而一个世纪以来，两者分别为完全不同的家族所占有。
奥地利丧失了大片省份，法国、英国已经上升到同样大的势力，普鲁士和俄国也已经形成；奥地利早已不再是那个在欧洲没有匹敌的君主国了。
已经形成了一种欧洲均势的体系，就是说，一种体系，靠它，通常欧洲所有的列强都对一场战争抱有兴趣，而每一个列强都被阻止去收获哪怕最顺利的战争的果实，无论是独自收获，还是哪怕只按它赢得的优势的比例来收获。
战争本身就已经如此大地改变了它们的性质，以致征服几个岛屿或一个省份，就要耗费多年的努力、巨额的钱财等等。

en: The idea of a universal monarchy has always been an empty word.

That it was not carried out when the plan had been formed shows the impossibility of its execution and thus the emptiness of this thought, but in more recent times there can no longer even be any talk of it.
zh: 普遍君主制这一观念，一直是一句空话。
它在计划已经形成的情况下却没有被实行，这表明它无法实行，因而也表明这种思想是空洞的，但在较近的时代，也根本不再谈得上这件事了。

en: Nevertheless Austria remains over-powerful in Germany, i.e. more powerful than any German estate is, more powerful than many of them together.
But at the same time Prussia has come into precisely this relation.
Austria and Prussia stand, with regard to a danger for the German estates, on the same rank.
That which one formerly called German freedom would have had to provide against both.
zh: 尽管如此，奥地利在德意志仍然过于强大，就是说，比任何一个德意志等级都更强大，比其中许多个加在一起还更强大。
但与此同时，普鲁士也进入了恰恰同样的这种关系。
就德意志各等级所面临的一种危险而言，奥地利和普鲁士处在同等的地位上。
人们从前所称的德意志自由，本来得对两者都加以防备。
